	The New York Yankees are heading towards another (likely) postseason run and the team has tapped one of New York’s most famous faces (and voices) to help root them on.

	Athleticwear brand Sportiqe has released a Billy Joel x New York Yankees collection, that pairs the brand’s T-shirts, sweatshirts and hoodies with Joel’s lyrics and the baseball team’s most famous motifs. A press release says the official collaboration “pairs the music of hometown legend Billy Joel with the energy, pride and unmistakable passion of New York fandom.”


	The Billy Joel x Yankees collection reworks one of the singer’s most famous lyrics as a rallying cry for the MLB team, with “New York State of Mind” printed on T-shirts, crewneck sweatshirts and on the back of a unisex hoodie. The navy blue Yankees logo is also featured prominently on each piece.

	Joel was born in the Bronx and the singer has had plenty of connections to the Yankees throughout his career, including a bestselling live album recorded during his two sold-out concerts at Yankee Stadium in 1990. That concert run is commemorated in a vintage-inspired T-shirt that is also part of the Sportiqe collection.

	Pricing for the official collaboration ranges from $52 to $109 with women’s sizes running small to XL and sizing for the unisex pieces running from XS to 3XL. You can shop the full collection here and see some of our favorites below.

	Depending on who you ask, Joel is generally considered more of a Mets fan. The singer’s 2008 Shea Stadium run was commemorated into a live album and DVD, titled “Live at Shea Stadium: The Concert.” The singer also famously played the final concert ever at Shea Stadium, a.k.a. “The Last Play at Shea.” 


	In addition to the Yankees collab, Sportiqe also has a Mets collection inspired by Joel, including a vintage-inspired T-shirt that commemorates Joel’s 2008 performance of “Piano Man.”

	The Mets have been mathematically eliminated from the playoffs this season. The Yankees, meantime, hold the first wild-card spot in the American League.

title: Newly Discovered Plant-Eating Insects Named After Taylor Swift
description: Taylor Swift, the award-winning billionaire singer and songwriter, is getting a new honor: The megastar is the namesake of several recently discover
body:
Taylor Swift, the award-winning billionaire singer and songwriter, is getting a new honor: The megastar is the namesake of several recently discovered species of plant-feeding insects from Australia.

	Researchers at the University of California, Riverside have named the new species of insect after Swift. A paper describing the 12 new species was published in the journal “Insect Systematics and Evolution.” Of these, one genus has been named Swiftiephylus, which combines “Swiftie,” the term for Swift’s fans, with “Phylus,” a name commonly used for this group of insects.
	

	Four species have been bestowed names inspired by the artist herself as well as several of her albums: Swiftiephylus taylorae, Swiftiephylus amator, Swiftiephylus intrepidus, and Swiftiephylus poetorum. The names are Latin versions of “Taylor,” “lover,” “fearless” and “poets,” respectively. 


	The Swiftiephylus insects are closely associated with Australian she-oaks, trees and shrubs adapted to environments ranging from tropical forests to coastal dunes and extreme heat, according to UC Riverside. Many plant bugs spend their entire lives on a particular host plant, from hatching through adulthood and egg laying.

	UC Riverside entomology doctoral student Sarah Schroeder decided to name the insects after Swift, in the hopes her association with the bugs will elevate both the insects and the concept of insect conservation more generally. “It felt authentic to me as a lifelong Swiftie to honor Taylor in this way, as well as bring attention to the diversity of insects that has yet to be discovered,” Schroeder said in a statement provided by the university.
	

	One of the reasons Schroeder dedicated the names of the new insects to Swift also has to do with their appearance: She believes their coloring helps them camouflage among she-oak flowers, which feature spindly red to orange structures. Similar cream-and-red coloration has been observed in distantly related bugs living on the same plants, suggesting camouflage may have evolved independently multiple times. “Taylor Swift’s iconic look is her blonde hair and red lips. These insects are pale yellow with accents of red throughout,” Schroeder said. “In the paper, I refer to them as blonde.”

	The new insects “are not known to be pests to either humans or animals,” according to UC Riverside. They are part of a family called Miridae, the largest family of true bugs, with more than 11,000 described species worldwide.

	Though the insects are new to science, the specimens themselves have been waiting decades to be formally described. They were among the plant bug specimens collected between 1995 and 2004 during a large biodiversity effort involving researchers from the American Museum of Natural History and Australian collaborators. The collecting effort yielded more than 50,000 specimens, many of which have required years of taxonomic work to sort, study and describe.

	“Taxonomy is the cornerstone of conservation,” Schroeder said. “If we don’t describe species, we don’t know they exist and can’t conserve them. Honoring Taylor through naming these species after her is a way to honor conservation science and bring attention to all the unknown diversity.”

	Variety has reached out to reps for Swift for any comment.

	UC Riverside’s bug researchers have named other species after celebs, including Jeff Daniels, who became the namesake of a tarantula-killing, hermaphroditic species of worm in 2022.

	Pictured above: Taylor Swift and one of the newly named Swiftiephylus bugs

title: Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Set to Open AFI Film Fest
description:

	It also marks the U.S premiere of the film. “Wildw
body:
Laika’s “Wildwood” is set to open the 40th edition of AFI Fest, presented by Canva, on Oct. 21.

	It also marks the U.S premiere of the film. “Wildwood” is the latest animated feature from the Portland-based studio Laika, and it’s directed and produced by Travis Knight.

	The film follows a young girl named Prue (Peyton Elizabeth Lee), who launches a desperate rescue mission and is joined by her classmate Curtis (Jacob Tremblay) to save her baby brother from a murder of crows. It’s a quest that takes her into a forbidden forest outside Portland, Oregon, that’s filled with enchanted creatures at every turn, from talking animals to bandits to other powerful figures.
	

	 The voice cast also features Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, Angela Bassett, Awkwafina, Jake Johnson, Charlie Day, Amandla Stenberg, Jemaine Clement, Maya Erskine, Tantoo Cardinal, Tom Waits and  Richard E. Grant.


	“AFI is honored to celebrate ‘Wildwood’ as the Opening Night Film of the 40th Annual AFI Fest,” says Bob Gazzale, AFI President and CEO. “At a time when the world needs artistic inspiration more than ever, ‘Wildwood’ comes to the rescue by inviting audiences to a handcrafted, endlessly imaginative world that both dazzles and delights.”

	Knight adds, “Sixteen years is a long time to carry a story with you. And yet, sometimes that’s what stories ask of the people who tell them. ‘Wildwood’ was built slowly, painstakingly, by hundreds of extraordinary artists and craftspeople who gave something of themselves to this movie. For so long, this strange and beautiful world belonged only to those of us fortunate enough to wander through it together. To finally emerge blinking into the daylight at AFI FEST is a profound honor.” He continues, “AFI has a long tradition of championing ambitious and distinctive filmmaking and the filmmakers with the audacity, imagination and occasional poor judgment to attempt something genuinely different and sincere. We’re grateful to be among them. For sixteen years, we’ve been finding our way through Wildwood. What a privilege it is to finally welcome others inside.”
	

	The 40th edition will take place from Oct. 21-25 and will feature a curated selection of red carpet premieres, special screenings, world cinema, documentaries and short films. Program highlights from last year’s AFI Fest included “Bugonia,” “Christy,” “Jay Kelly,” “The Testament of Ann Lee” and more.

title: ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race UK: All Stars’ Set to Premiere on WOW Presents Plus (EXCLUSIVE)

	The news comes after The Sun
body:
“RuPaul’s Drag Race UK” is moving from the BBC and headed to World of Wonder‘s streaming platform WOW Presents Plus. 

	The news comes after The Sun reported that the show would be leaving the BBC as part of its cuts.

	However, Variety can confirm that in Fall 2027, the franchise will return with the first ever “RuPaul’s Drag Race UK: All Stars,” celebrating the artistry of the Queens who have worked the U.K. runway.


	The show’s eighth season, which just launched on BBC 3 scored its second-highest-rated premiere in the history of the franchise, trailing only Season 6 (which scored 9.0). The show bowed to an 8.8 IMDB rating with viewership up 20% on the streaming platform WOW Presents Plus.
	

	This herstoric season of “All Stars” will be available globally on WOW Presents Plus including, for the first time, in the U.K. Subscribers will be able to stream all eight seasons of “RuPaul’s Drag Race UK” and all three seasons of “RuPaul’s Drag Race UK Vs The World.”

	The successful launch of Season 8 follows a record-breaking run of the global franchise.

	The main show, “RuPaul’s Drag Race,” recently finished its 18th season and was the most watched season in the franchise’s history.  Myki Meeks didn’t have the strongest start to the season, but after her fellow queens placed her at the bottom of the “Rate-A-Queen” twist, she exacted her revenge. In the end, it was Meeks who sashayed her way to the top and was crowned the winner of “RuPaul’s Drag Race” Season 18. The show also landed 11 Emmy nominations for Season 18 and its aftershow, “RuPaul’s Drag Race: Untucked.”
	

	The franchise continued to expand and grow with new seasons and formats of “Canada’s Drag Race,” “Drag Race Down Under,” “Drag Race Mexico” and “Drag Race France.” All premiered with significant double digit growth.

	These milestones have been achieved at a challenging time and in an uncertain political climate. In a statement, co-founders of World of Wonder and “Drag Race” producers Fenton Bailey and Randy Barbato said, “Historically, during times of anxiety and regression, the queer, trans and drag communities are often targeted. Today is no exception. We at World of Wonder are so grateful to our members for their support, and we remain steadfast in the values that make ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race’ more than just a fiercely entertaining show. For millions, it’s a lifeline, a safe space and a celebration, and WOW Presents Plus is incredibly proud to keep providing that platform.”

title: Jaafar Jackson, Inde Navarrette and Ray Nicholson Among Variety’s 10 Actors to Watch for 2026

body:
Variety has unveiled its 2026 class of 10 Actors to Watch.

	Since 1998, the franchise has singled out breakout performers on the cusp of the industry’s front ranks and the track record speaks for itself. Past honorees include more than 35 Oscar winners and nominees, among them Mahershala Ali, Timothée Chalamet and Brie Larson.

	Last year’s 2025 class already made good on their honors. Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas landed a supporting actress Oscar nomination for the Norwegian familial drama “Sentimental Value.” Chase Infiniti followed “One Battle After Another” with an Emmy nomination for lead drama actress this year for Hulu’s “The Testaments,” while Miles Caton broke through as both performer and songwriter in Ryan Coogler’s horror smash “Sinners.”
	

	This year’s honorees were co-programmed by Clayton Davis, chief awards editor and Emily Longeretta, director of features. The 10 breakout sensations will be profiled in the Oct. 7 issue of Variety and will be celebrated at an Oct. 18 in-person brunch at the Newport Beach Film Festival Honors. 


	“Partnering with Variety to spotlight the 10 Actors to Watch is one of the highlights of our year,” says Gregg Schwenk, CEO and co-founder of the Newport Beach Film Festival. “This group is proof of what’s next — actors with the range, the instincts and the presence to define the next era of film and television. We couldn’t be more honored to be hosting this incredible group of emerging talent at the 27th Annual Newport Beach Film Festival Honors Brunch this year.”

	This year’s 10 Actors to Watch are:
	

	Esmé Creed-MilesPlays the unfiltered and charismatic Marianne Dashwood in Georgia Oakley’s “Sense and Sensibility” for Focus Features.

	Mariana Di GirólamoCo-stars in Martin McDonagh’s dramedy “Wild Horse Nine” for Searchlight Pictures, opposite John Malkovich and Steve Buscemi.

	Rosalind EleazarLeads Chris Rock’s A24 industry dramedy “Misty Green” and returns as Louisa Guy in the sixth season of Apple TV’s espionage drama “Slow Horses.”

	GuitarricadelafuenteStars in the Netflix Spanish-language epic “La Bola Negra” and appears in Pedro Almodóvar’s “Bitter Christmas” for Sony Pictures Classics.

	Summer H. Howell Will take on the title role in Prime Video’s horror series “Carrie” and will appear in James Clayton’s “Runaway.”

	Jaafar JacksonStars as Michael Jackson in Lionsgate’s billion-dollar blockbuster “Michael” and is filming David Gordon Green’s “Supermax” opposite Will Smith.

	Ruth MadeleyPlays disability rights activist Judy Heumann in Sian Heder’s biopic drama “Being Heumann” for Apple Original Films.

	Inde Navarrette The breakout played Nikki in the Focus Features horror sensation “Obsession,” which led to her casting as the superhero Rogue in Marvel Studios’ upcoming “X-Men” film. 

	Ray Nicholson Plays a football player turned war hero in Peter Berg’s “The Mosquito Bowl,” following his role in the FX thriller series “The Beauty.”

	Joseph ZadaTakes on Haymitch Abernathy in Lionsgate’s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” and plays Cal Trask in Netflix’s limited drama series “East of Eden.”

title: Apple Introduces iPhone Duo, Its First Foldable Smartphone
description:
Apple is giving a new twist to its flagship smartphone line: The company unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone.

	The company’s iPh
body:
Apple is giving a new twist to its flagship smartphone line: The company unveiled the iPhone Duo, its first foldable smartphone.

	The company’s iPhone Duo foldable has an internal dual-display panel that provides the largest, most immersive screen size ever at 7.6 inches diagonally — and it’s also the thinnest iPhone ever, according to Apple. (When unfolded, it looks like a small iPad tablet.) There’s also a screen on the outside of the device. 
	

	The iPhone Duo is priced starting at $1,999 with 256 gigabytes of storage, ranging up to $3,199 for a model with 2 terabytes. Preorders start Oct. 16 and the device will begin shipping Oct. 23. It’s available in two colors, dubbed “star white” and “night sky.”


	According to Apple, a few third-party apps — including Netflix, Zoom and Slack — are already taking advantage of the folding design to take advantage of the larger display. Apple is releasing software development kits for developers to design (or redesign) their apps for the iPhone Duo.

	Apple’s iPhone Duo launch Wednesday comes seven years to the day after Samsung shipped its first foldable smartphone, the Galaxy Fold, in September 2019.

	Along with the Duo, the company also announced the single-screen iPhone 18 baseline model and Pro 18 and Pro Max 18 versions, as well as AirPods 5 and updated versions of the Apple Watch with enhanced health-sensing features. It was the first product launch presided over by newly installed CEO John Ternus, formerly Apple’s head of hardware engineering, who took over from Tim Cook at the helm of the tech giant as of Sept. 1.
	

	Other foldable designs feel like “two phones that have been stuck together,” Ternus said. He called the iPhone Duo “the most transformational change to iPhone since the original. With an entirely new design and intuitive experiences, it shows what’s possible when hardware and software are engineered together and redefines what it means to use a foldable phone.”

	When it’s closed, the 5.4-inch outer display of the iPhone Duo delivers 90% of the screen area of iPhone 18 Pro in a “pocketable” design. Lock-screen controls and app navigation and controls are located on the side of the iPhone Duo, to “maximize vertical space for content,” Apple said. 

	When the phone is open, the display shows two home-screen pages with Today View (a vertically scrolling list of customizable widgets) on the left. With the “Split View” feature, you can launch two different apps on the left and right screens for side-by-side comparison; you can also drop-and-drop items between the two sides.



	

									Courtesy of Apple
	



	The company said iOS 27 is tailored for iPhone Duo. The operating system “seamlessly adapts to the new ways to use iPhone Duo — content reacts as it folds, reorients when turned to the side and switches to the appropriate display when flipped over,” per Apple.

	Apple said iPhone Duo has new camera features that are possible only with foldable design, such as the ability to take a selfie with the higher-resolution rear cameras and preview the shot on the outer display.

	iPhone Duo provides enhanced battery life, too, with up to 31 hours of video playback when using the inner display and up to 44 hours of video playback when using the outer display. It provides up to 24 hours of usage per charge when both displays are used equally, according to Apple.

	Apple also touted AI features for the new iPhones, which act as “your intelligent personal hub,” Ternus said in a video played at the top of the event. He underscored that its Apple Intelligence AI features — including an upgraded Siri AI app that has more “expressive” voices — run locally on the device whenever possible to protect users’ data privacy.

title: Dolly Parton Hid Cancer Battle From ‘A Lot of Family,’ Not Just Fans: ‘She Did Not Want People Sad’ and ‘Could Not Bear Negative Things’
description: Dolly Parton‘s sister Stella told “CBS Mornings” in a new interview that the country music icon hid her cancer battle not only from fans but also fr
body:
Dolly Parton‘s sister Stella told “CBS Mornings” in a new interview that the country music icon hid her cancer battle not only from fans but also from “a lot of family” because she did not want her legacy tainted with sadness. Parton died in Nashville on Aug. 25 at 80 years old. The singer’s representative later confirmed her death followed a “brief battle” with cancer. The news came as a shock to both Parton’s friends and family. 

	“Dolly did not want anybody to tell that because Dolly could not bear negative things,” Stella told “CBS Mornings” co-host Gayle King. “She would not have wanted her fans worried about it… She didn’t want a lot of the family worried about it. Some of us knew, the ones that were closer, but not every relative.”
	

	“She did not want people sad,” Sella continued. “She’d be really happy and delighted that people have shown her so much love because she knew that that would make us feel better as her family. Bottom line, end of the day, her family and Carl’s family and probably Judy’s family are the people that she would want to say, ‘See, everything I did, they cared. They really loved me.’” 

	Stella was referring to Dolly’s late husband, Carl Dean, and her longtime best friend, Judy Ogle.

	While Parton had been public with her health issues over the last year, it had not been disclosed she was battling cancer until after her death. She appeared on video a week before to introduce the a new roller coaster at Dollywood theme park after canceling her in-person appearance due to dizziness and dehydration. Parton canceled a six-show residency in Las Vegas last year due to “health challenges,” then also canceled the rescheduled dates this May. 
	

	“My immune system and my digestive system got all out of whack over the past couple, three years, and they’re working real hard on rebuilding [and] strengthening those, and hopefully I’ll be up to snuff again soon,” Parton explained at the time.

	Stella Parton’s full interview with “CBS Mornings” will air on Thursday, Sept. 10.

title: ‘La La Land’ Shines Again at Venice Film Festival With Performance Led by Justin Hurwitz, Presented by Cartier
description: Ten years after its world premiere at the 2016 Venice International Film Festival, “La La Land” is back for a victory lap with “La La Land in Concer
body:
Ten years after its world premiere at the 2016 Venice International Film Festival, “La La Land” is back for a victory lap with “La La Land in Concert.” The celebratory 10th anniversary screening, complete with a live-to-film concert, took place on Sept. 5 during the 83rd edition of La Biennale de Venezia. The award-winning film was broadcast alongside a live orchestra performance of the soundtrack inside the iconic Venice institution Teatro La Fenice, one of the most renowned opera houses in the city.  
	

	Presented by the Cartier Cinema Club in collaboration with Lionsgate and Hurwitz Concerts, the event was attended by the film’s writer and director, Damien Chazelle, and his close collaborator and friend, the film’s composer Justin Hurwitz, who conducted the Orchestra Regionale Filarmonia Veneta. The pair share a lifelong friendship that spans multiple projects, but “La La Land” is their most successful collaboration by far. Hurwitz won several awards for his work on the film, including Best Original Score and Best Original Song for “City of Stars.” 

	“To conduct an orchestra along with ‘La La Land’ in Venice, where the world first saw [the film] 10 years ago, is an absolute dream come true,” said Hurwitz, who conducted the prestigious Italian orchestra known for both their classical work and high-profile collaborations with pop stars and prominent performers.

	The orchestra was joined by a special player — pianist Randy Kerber, a studio legend and prolific cinematic composer who performed on the film’s original soundtrack recording. Prior to “La La Land,” the accomplished musician has worked on over 800 films, including “Titanic” and “Forrest Gump,” and brought the film’s signature jazz piano riffs to life at the screening. A decade after premiering in competition in Venice on Aug. 31, 2016, “La La Land” remains a unique accomplishment in the contemporary cinematic landscape. It’s rare for a modern musical to elicit the kind of acclaim it received, and the outpouring of public support from the public that followed its success is equally unusual. Moreover, it’s already proven to stand the test of time. Even after a decade, the film is just as relevant and resonant. 
	

	Alberto Barbera, the artistic director of the cinema department at the Venice International Film Festival, defines “La La Land” as the “finest musical of the contemporary era.” In his view, it’s the only modern musical that’s capable of standing alongside timeless classics from Hollywood’s Golden Age. “La La Land is a captivating and spectacular film, an unforgettable love story, a heartfelt love letter to Hollywood cinema, a celebration of creativity and a remarkably mature reflection on the nature of success and failure,” Barbera said. “Above all, however, it features some of the most beautiful songs and musical compositions of recent years. That is why the opportunity to experience it once again, accompanied by the live performance of the Orchestra Regionale Filarmonia Veneta, is truly unmissable, a gift for everyone who fell in love with the film, as well as for the few who have yet to discover it.”

	The screening was offered free to the public and represented the festival’s desire to offer events that benefit not just international attendees, but the local community as well. Inside the Teatro la Fenice, gilded Rococo interiors and lavish gold decor framed the film with glittering allure, adding a dramatic subtext to its rags-to-riches storyline. 

	“La La Land in Concert” was just the kind of special event that Cartier’s Cinema Club strives to organize to support and amplify artists and filmmakers. “The Cartier Cinema Club is conceived as a platform for ongoing dialogue and discovery,” said Arnaud Carrez, senior vice president and chief marketing officer of Cartier. “We want to continue celebrating the many talents who contribute to filmmaking, both in front of and behind the camera, through screenings, conversations, masterclasses and other creative formats. Our ambition is to develop the Cinema Club internationally while giving each edition its own identity, reflecting the creative energy and cultural context of the city where it takes place. What will remain constant is our commitment to celebrating creativity, craftsmanship and the collective spirit behind cinema.”

	Set against the venue’s spectacular neoclassical trimmings, hand-painted frescoes and Murano glass chandeliers, the most impressive element of the “La La Land” anniversary screening was still the live orchestra, a living, breathing layer that enriched each scene with grand swells and swift decrescendos. Bathed in the shifting light from the screen, the orchestra’s movements and playing functioned like a second drama unfolding onstage, augmenting and mirroring the original film. 
	

	The special concert event reflects Cartier’s year-round support of the work at the Fondazione Teatro la Fenice; the brand will also sponsor its upcoming season of opera, ballet and concerts. Since the 2021 Venice International Film Festival, Maison Cartier has supported a host of initiatives that aim to protect the city’s living heritage, namely by contributing to the ongoing development of Venice’s cultural life.

	“Cartier’s relationship with cinema goes back more than a century, so supporting the Venice Film Festival is a very natural expression of this heritage,” Arnaud Carrez said. “Since 2021, our partnership with the festival has allowed us to deepen this relationship and to support contemporary cinema and the people who bring it to life. Venice is particularly meaningful because the festival is the oldest film festival in the world and one of the most prestigious. We share its fundamental values of creativity, excellence and savoir-faire.”

	Along with the Cinema Club, Arnaud Carrez also noted the brand’s Glory to the Filmmaker Award and masterclass conversations as ancillary initiatives at Venice this year. “Our ambition is not simply to be present at the festival, but to make a meaningful contribution to its creative ecosystem,” he said.

	“La La Land In Concert” is just one of many events and collaborations Cartier has undertaken to showcase the collective spirit of cinema and add to the Venice International Film Festival’s rich, multifaceted history. Along with the concert, there was the inaugural Cartier Cinema Club dinner held at the Gritti Palace, where Chazelle and “La La Land” were honored with a dinner overlooking the Basilica della Salute. 

	“Our commitment to Venice extends well beyond cinema. We want to contribute to preserving the city’s extraordinary artistic heritage while supporting the people and institutions that keep its culture alive,” Arnaud Carrez said of Cartier’s initiatives to protect the living heritage of Venice and continue the development of the city’s cultural life.

	“We support the restoration of parts of the Teatro Verde, the historic open-air amphitheater on the island of San Giorgio Maggiore, and we have an ongoing relationship with Teatro La Fenice, supporting its cultural program,” Arnaud Carrez shared. “We are also working with Orsoni Venezia 1888 and La Scola to support the transmission of traditional Venetian mosaic craftsmanship. At Cartier, we always talk about living heritage because it needs to be preserved, transmitted to new generations and given the opportunity to evolve. This is also aligned with our own approach to craftsmanship and savoir-faire.”

title: ‘A Good Little Soldier’ Review: Alba Rohrwacher Goes Corporate Drone in Stéphane Brizé’s Lukewarm Workplace Drama
description: There’s not a single moment in Stéphane Brizé’s lukewarm workplace drama “A Good Little Soldier” where Alba Rohrwacher’s Carla Moretti isn’t at work
body:
There’s not a single moment in Stéphane Brizé’s lukewarm workplace drama “A Good Little Soldier” where Alba Rohrwacher’s Carla Moretti isn’t at work — or on her way to the office, or at a coffee shop around the corner where she could scurry right back. Bowing in Venice’s main competition, and Brizé’s fourth time on the Lido, the film in many ways challenges the clichés we have about labor and the French, with their seemingly infinite congés and tendency to stop-drop-and-protest at the first sign of abuse. As the title suggests, Carla doesn’t just endure her job’s outsized demands on her time, energy, and soul, but is a workhorse by choice: a person willingly stripped of personality and independence like the sleek commercial everyplace (in fact, Paris’s anachronistically modern 13th arrondissement) where the story unfolds. Unfortunately, the film, too, could use a bit of punch to lift it out of the humdrum anti-corporate critique it takes for granted to be novel. 
	

	Essentially just a character study about the drone mindset, albeit one given decent texture by Rohrwacher’s performance, the film follows Carla in the first weeks of her new job as the human resources manager at a health insurance firm led by swaggering CEO Arnaud (a devilish Vincent Lindon, in his sixth film with Brizé). In a nervy boardroom sequence early on, Carla and her fellow executives present Arnaud with a glossy corporate video meant to attract a new generation of suits with inclusive messaging and feelgood images of able-bodied employees working alongside disabled ones. 
	

	A rat-a-tat drum score and fidgety handheld camerawork gives a cheeky, satirical edge to Arnaud’s ensuing tantrum, where he rails against the video’s political correctness with the arrogance of a so-called truth-teller. The video should attract “winners,” the celebration of strength over weakness, the cornerstone of a corporate mandate that privileges profit-generating at all costs and fosters cutthroat attitudes that embrace this goal. 

	After Arnaud’s traumatizing tirade, Brizé shifts the focus entirely to Carla, who is now tense with imposter syndrome that perversely pushes her to work even harder — she knew the video was “creepy,” too. Brizé’s script, co-written by Coralie Amédéo and Olivier Gorce, sticks to low-hanging fruit in its mockery of corporate life, as Carla supervises the filming of a new video conceived by a pseudo-auteur, as well as actually “creepy” team-building workshops that double as humiliation rituals. 

	Brizé weaves between these absurd moments and two slow-simmering crises that cause Carla to begin doubting her diehard commitment to work. Carla has co-custody of her son Louis (Adrien Bobinet) with ex-husband Olivier (David Talbot), though recently she’s been canceling or pushing back her weeks. Louis sends Carla daily video missives that she listens to during her commute, otherwise the two video chat while Carla eats takeout in the office — and only half these talks are pleasant because Carla fixates on his mediocre math scores. While tender Olivier dedicates every weekend to fun activities with his son, Carla doesn’t realize she’s pushing him away. It’s hardly worth it. Carla’s biggest breakthrough at work is coming up with a banal slogan: “Care for our customers, care for our employees.”

	Brizé’s refusal to show Carla in any other context outside of work gives the film a stale, claustrophobic quality, as if she’s permanently locked away at a distance — as far from her son across the city as the New York friend she Zooms with. These people are satellites with glitchy connections, half-humans whose voices she can turn off with a push of the sound button. 

	Meanwhile, Carla receives a voice recording that proves that one of the company’s most efficient team leaders, Madame Lalouette (Carine Rouvier), has been verbally abusing the timid Madame Morel (Sandra Le Gall). Knowing that Madame Lalouette’s sales numbers are too high to fire her, Carla attempts to transfer Madame Morel to a different department — a move that irritates her superiors and highlights her weakness. Madame Morel may be meeting her target sales, but everyone else in her team has been overperforming, which is enough of a reason to get rid of her and the liability problem she represents. 
	

	Notwithstanding one comically exaggerated outburst where Carla loses it while tele-tutoring Louis, Rohrwacher’s precision allows Carla the subtlest evolution— though perhaps too subtle to have much of a dramatic impact in a story where the titular soldier follows orders down to the very last frame. We notice flickers of a moral conscience begin to shine through Carla’s anodyne professionalism, but is that enough? Awareness-raising never is.

schema.headline: ‘A Good Little Soldier’ Review: Alba Rohrwacher Goes Corporate Drone in Stéphane Brizé’s Lukewarm Workplace Drama

body:
Sep 9, 2026 11:00am PT	
	


	And 'Harry Potter'!
	
			


			
			
	

									Peacock, Apple, Netflix, CBS
	

		
	
				

	Yes, peak TV is over — but we challenge you even to begin watching all the great shows that will premiere in the coming weeks, or even catch up with the new good ones that came out this summer. Are you all caught up on “Furious” on Hulu and “Sterling Point” on Prime Video and HBO’s “Lanterns” and Netflix’s “My Brilliant Career”? We didn’t think so! (Whispers: Neither are we.)

	Just since September started a mere nine days ago, Season 2 of “The Gentlemen” and FX’s “The Drop: A Snowfall Saga” both premiered. What we’re saying is, peak TV or not, there continues to be an embarrassment of riches across television, and that will continue this fall, as you will see below. (Shout out to the actual show “Below,” where Josh Hartnett plays a small-town fisherman battling a sea monster! We’ve been too scared to watch the screeners, but will soon.)

	This list doesn’t include everything, of course. There are shows that haven’t been dated, like Netflix’s highly anticipated “Pride & Prejudice” remake, starring Emma Corrin as Lizzy Bennet. And several network shows that typically come out in the fall, such as CBS’ “Matlock” and ABC’s “High Potential,” will be premiering midseason. As for network staples we know you’ll find on your own, there’s Fox’s “Best Medicine” and “Doc” double feature, premiering on Sept. 22; CBS’ “Marshals” and “Tracker” on Oct. 4; “Abbott Elementary” has its Season 6 (six! where does the time go?) premiere on Oct. 7; the One Chicago shows premiere on Oct. 7; “Law & Order: SVU” and “Law & Order” on Oct. 8; ABC’s “9-1-1,” “9-1-1: Nashville” and “Grey’s Anatomy” premiere on Oct. 15; and NBC brings back “St. Denis Medical” for Season 3 and “The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins” for Season 2 on Nov. 2.

	“South America” — the artist formerly known as “South Park” — has already entered the zeitgeist before its Sept. 16 premiere on Comedy Central, with its Emmys win and Trump-mocking name change; the docuseries “Jay-Z in 8” premieres on Sept. 18 (but missed our cutoff for inclusion); Netflix’s Omar Sy-starring series “Lupin: Part 4” returns for the first time since 2023 on Oct. 23, and Season 2 of the streamer’s delightful spy thriller “Black Doves,” starring Keira Knightley, will drop on Nov. 5; Season 4 of “Tulsa King” premieres on Paramount+ on Oct. 16 — and, last but not least, Season 3 of “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” returns to Disney+ on Nov. 20.

	One last disclosure: Obviously, Christmas will bring the series premiere of HBO’s “Harry Potter,” and that is decidedly … in the winter. This is an inarguable fact! But given that the show is going to be one of the biggest pop culture events of the year, and will also fuel the discourse machine because of J.K. Rowling,  we just had to include it. Please don’t place us under one of the unforgivable curses; we only mean to serve.

	Enough of these ramblings! Let’s get to the list.


			
			
	Last Seen
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Apple TV				
					
				

	Sept. 9, Apple TV

	An Australian thriller led by Patrick Brammall, “Last Seen” is an adaptation of Ryan David Jahn’s book “The Dispatcher” and follows police detective Ian Ridley. He refuses to believe that his daughter is really gone 11 years after her disappearance. Per the logline, “When he receives a distress call from a teenage girl he is certain is Maggie, he will stop at nothing to find her and reunite his broken family, whatever the cost.”

	Cast: Patrick Brammall, Maxine Peake, Brendan Cowell, Daniel Henshall, Zahra Newman, Jessica Wren, Tobias Muhafidin and Chloe Jean Lourdes

		
			
			
	The Paper
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of John P. Fleenor/Peacock				
					
				

	Sept. 9, Peacock

	“The Office” spinoff returns for its second season with another journalism journey for Domhnall Gleeson’s Ned. Plus, romance could be in the air with him and Chelsea Frei’s Mare. To add to the fun, this season will feature guest stars Jon Lovitz and Andy Richter.

	Cast: Domhnall Gleeson, Sabrina Impacciatore, Chelsea Frei, Melvin Gregg, Tim Key, Ramona Young, Eric Rahill, Duane Shepard Sr. and Alex Edelman

		
			
			
	The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives
			
								
				

	Sept. 10, Hulu

	While “The Bachelorette” is still nowhere to be found, “TSLOMW” will live on! Taylor Frankie Paul returns from filming the dating show in this five-episode fifth season and her life quickly flips upside down. Plus, Whitney Leavitt heads to Broadway and the headlines never stop coming out of Utah.

	Cast: Taylor Frankie Paul, Jen Affleck, Jessi Draper, Layla Taylor, Mayci Neeley, Mikayla Matthews, Miranda Hope and Whitney Leavitt

		
			
			
	Colin From Accounts
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Lisa Tomasetti/Paramount+				
					
				

	Sept. 10, Paramount+

	The third and final season of the cult-favorite romantic comedy picks up after the Season 2 cliffhanger of Gordon’s unexpected proposal to Ashley. “Even as life moves on, with challenges at work, ongoing family battles and new friendship dramas, something keeps pulling this flawed, funny pair back into each other’s orbits,” the logline reads. “Do Gordon and Ashley belong together – or is their beloved dog Colin the only thing keeping their futures intertwined?”

	Cast: Patrick Brammall (again!), Harriet Dyer, Thomas Cocquerel, Nikki Shiels, Mark Trevorrow, Emma Harvie, Genevieve Hegney, Michael Logo, Helen Thomson, Darren Gilshenan, Virginia Gay, Annie Maynard, Celeste Barber, Justin Rosniak and Tai Hara

		
			
			
	Crew Girl
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Craig Minielly/Netflix				
					
				

	Sept. 10, Netflix

	Netflix dives headfirst into the YA genre with a story about Teagan Tao (Miku Martineau), a 16-year-old competitive rower whose life is changed by a family scandal. She’s forced to relocate to a prestigious East Coast school, where she must join “the school’s notoriously dysfunctional boys’ varsity crew as their coxswain” since there’s no girls’ team. Add in complicated family dynamics, competitive rivalries and, of course, unexpected romance.

	Cast: Miku Martineau, Jessica Paré, Sam Braun, Kyle Clark and Thomas Cadrot

		
			
			
	Agatha Christie’s Tommy and Tuppence
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of BritBox				
					
				

	Sept. 15, BritBox

	The first contemporary English-language Agatha Christie TV series adaptation follows Tuppence and Tommy, two complete opposites who make up a detective duo — and who happen to be in a playful romance. The premiere (on Christie’s birthday!) will bookend BritBox’s “Eras of Agatha Christie” event, streaming her many adaptations to celebrate her legacy.

	Cast: Antonia Thomas, Josh Dylan, Imelda Staunton, Nicholas Richardson, Charlie Candou, Callie Cooke and Chizzy Akudolu

		
			
			
	Dancing With the Stars
			
										
					Image Credit: Disney				
					
				

	Sept. 15, ABC

	After the massive 34th season of “Dancing With the Stars,” the competition reality juggernaut returns. Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough and Bruno Tonioli are back as judges while Julianne Hough and Alfonso Ribeiro will once again host. Pro Sharna Burgess is set to make her return this year for her first season since 2021, and last year’s winner, Witney Carson, is back — this time, competing while pregnant.

	Cast: Ciara Miller, Maura Higgins, Guillermo Rodriguez, Jackson Olson — here’s the full list! 

		
			
			
	Slow Horses
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Jack English/Apple TV				
					
				

	Sept. 16, Apple TV

	The critically acclaimed hit is back — as is fan-favorite Sid Baker, played by Olivia Cooke. In the sixth season, adapted from Mick Herron’s “Joe Country” and “Slough House,” Diana Taverner (Kristin Scott Thomas) leads the group into “a fatally high-stakes game of retaliation and revenge.”

	Cast: Gary Oldman, Kristin Scott Thomas, Jack Lowden, Saskia Reeves, Christopher Chung, Aimee-Ffion Edwards, Rosalind Eleazar, Joanna Scanlan, Samuel West, Ruth Bradley, Tom Brooke, Jonathan Pryce, Hugo Weaving, Lenny Rush and Olivia Cooke

		
			
			
	Neagley
			
										
					Image Credit: Shane Mahood/Prime				
					
				

	Sept. 16, Prime Video

	Following the “Reacher” Season 4 finale, all eight episodes of the spinoff will be available to stream. The series, based on characters created in Lee Child’s novels, follows private investigator Frances Neagley in Chicago, a former protégé of Jack Reacher. Per the official logline, “When she learns that a beloved friend from her past has been killed in a suspicious accident, she becomes hell-bent on justice. Using everything she’s learned from Jack Reacher and her time as a member of the 110 Special Investigators, Neagley puts herself on a dangerous path to uncover a menacing evil.”

	Cast: Maria Sten, Greyston Holt, Adeline Rudolph, Jasper Jones, Matthew Del Negro and Damon Herriman; Alan Ritchson guest stars as Jack Reacher. 

		
			
			
	Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix				
					
				

	Sept. 17, Netflix

	Ryan Murphy’s “Monster” universe continues, this time telling “the story of how one young woman changed what the world believed a killer could be… all it took was an axe.” The “monster” in question for the fourth installment is Lizzie Borden, a repressed daughter of a wealthy family who bonds with her rebellious maid. “Trapped in a house built on humiliation and cruelty, they escape into a fantasy of sex, power and revenge,” the logline reads, as the series dives into the gruesome unsolved murders and the events that led to the act.

	Cast: Ella Beatty, Vicky Krieps, Charlie Hunnam, Rebecca Hall, Billie Lourd, Joey Pollari, Sarah Paulson and Jessica Barden

		
			
			
	The Traitors: New Blood
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Euan Cherry/NBC				
					
				

	Sept. 18, NBC

	While the celebrity version may be all the rage on Peacock, NBC is now joining the party with the first U.S. all-civilian rendition of the competition series. Emmy-winner Alan Cumming will, of course, return as host extraordinaire, and the premiere will be a super-sized two-hour episode.

	Cast: Alan Cumming, Abbey Benjamin​, Abby Lee​, Arisa Thomas​, Ben McDonnell​, Clyde Moser, Jay Vinnedge​, Joe Vanella​, Katie Fites​, Kim Daily​, Kriste Lewis​, Logan Smith, Madeline Kostopulos​, Mark Zgoda​, Michael Foote, Morgan Cook​, Niyyah Hayes​, Shane Beatty​, Sherry Kuehl, Tomica Adams​, Victor Vollbrechthausen​, Wyatt Gillespie​ and Xavier Scruggs 

		
			
			
	MobLand
			
										
					Image Credit: Luke Varley/Paramount+				
					
				

	Sept. 18, Paramount+

	Despite the behind-the-scenes drama — it was initially reported that Tom Hardy dropped out, but he later cleared things up and is back in — the Harrigan family is back for the second season. In Season 2, they face new rivals who threaten the family’s criminal empire. Per the logline, “as violence spills into every corner of their lives, loyalties snap, safety proves temporary, and the battle for power leaves no room for mercy.”

	Cast: Tom Hardy, Pierce Brosnan, Helen Mirren, Paddy Considine, Joanne Froggatt, Lara Pulver, Anson Boon, Mandeep Dhillon, Jasmine Jobson, Teddie Allen, Emmett J. Scanlan, Johnny Flynn, Ophelia Lovibond, Janet McTeer and Toby Jones.

		
			
			
	Outlander: Blood of My Blood
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Robert Wilson/Starz				
					
				

	Sept. 18, Starz

	While the flagship series has come to an end, the prequel is back for Season 2, following the parents of Claire and Jamie, decades before “Outlander” began. This season, two couples — Brian Fraser and Ellen MacKenzie, and Henry and Julia Beauchamp — will be torn apart by powers out of their control. Get ready to venture back to the Highlands of 18th-century Scotland.

	Cast: Jeremy Irvine, Hermione Corfield, Jamie Roy, Harriet Slater, Tony Curran, Séamus McLean Ross, Sam Retford, Rory Alexander and Conor MacNeill

		
			
			
	American Hostage
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Steven Ackerman/MGM+/Sony Pictures Television				
					
				

	Sept. 21, MGM+

	Based on a true story — and the scripted podcast of the same name, hosted by star Jon Hamm — the psychological thriller set in the 1970s tells the story of Fred Heckman, a beloved radio reporter who becomes the story when a man, Tony Kiritsis, demands to be interviewed while holding another man at gunpoint. Shawn Ryan and Eileen Myers (“The Night Agent”) produce.

	Cast: Jon Hamm, Giovanni Ribisi, Kristoffer Polaha, William Jackson Harper, Mireille Enos, Jonathan Tucker and Kat Cunning  

		
			
			
	Line of Fire
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Scott Gries/NBC				
					
				

	Sept. 21, NBC

	Your next family drama-procedural mashup obsession has arrived. Created by Joshua Safran (“Quantico,” “Gossip Girl”), “Line of Fire” follows a family of law enforcement agents — one from the FBI, one U.S. Marshal, a member of the Secret Service and a Department of Justice member — who must find a way to coexist. The season kicks off with what appears to be a cut-and-dry case that quickly turns into much more.

	Cast: Peter Krause, Hope Davis, Kat Cunning, Tommy O’Brien, Taylor Bloom and Charlie Barnett

		
			
			
	Wonka’s the Golden Ticket
			
										
					Image Credit: COURTESY OF NETFLIX				
					
				

	Sept. 23, Netflix

	Inspired by Roald Dahl’s book “Charlie & the Chocolate Factory,” this competition series with 12 Golden Ticket winners (and their partners) heading into Wonka’s Chocolate Factory to compete in the ultimate challenges. “Once inside, contestants must navigate a series of Wonka’s games, tests, and temptations designed to challenge them physically, mentally and morally,” the logline reads. “In this high-stakes social experiment, players will journey through the factory’s wondrous and unpredictable landscape, adapting, strategizing, and withstanding the unknown while proving they have the instincts, resilience, and character to thrive in chaos.”

	Plus, Gene Wilder’s Willy Wonka voice will be recreated, and Rusty Goffe, an original Oompa Loompa from the film, will be back.

		
			
			
	Brothers
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Ryan Green/Apple TV				
					
				

	Sept. 23, Apple TV

	Longtime, real-life best friends Woody Harrelson and Matthew McConaughey play fictionalized versions of themselves in this comedy, during which their characters find out they may be actual brothers. Throw in an identity crisis, some family drama — and a possible political run.

	Cast: Woody Harrelson, Matthew McConaughey, Natalie Martinez, Brittany Ishibashi, Nolan Almeida, Ella Grace Helton, Noah Carganilla, Highdee Kuan, Oona Yaffe and Holland Taylor

		
			
			
	A Different World
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of ELI JOSHUA ADE/Netflix				
					
				

	Sept. 24, Netflix

	A sequel series to the 1987 NBC “Cosby Show” spinoff, this version of “A Different World” follows college freshman Deborah (Maleah Joi Moon), the daughter of Whitley Gilbert and Dwayne Wayne. The show will feature many legacy characters returning, while also introducing a group of new friends for Deborah, as she tries to escape her parents’ shadows at Hillman College.

	Cast: Maleah Joi Moon, Alijah Kai, Cornell Young IV, Jordan Aaron Hall, Kennedi Reece, Chibuikem Uche, Jasmine Guy​, Kadeem Hardison​, Cree Summer and Darryl M. Bell

		
			
			
	American Horror Story
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of FX				
					
				

	Sept. 24, FX

	With the 13th season of “American Horror Story,” Ryan Murphy and Brad Falchuck are going big with 13 half-hour episodes. The season will include many fan-favorite characters from the last 12 seasons, including Constance Langdon, Cordelia Goode, Madison Montgomery, Marie Laveau, Rubber Man, Twisty the Clown and Kai Anderson; expect some of them to be in scenes together — even when the same actor is playing them.

	Cast: Sarah Paulson, Evan Peters, Angela Bassett, Kathy Bates, Emma Roberts, Billie Lourd, Gabourey Sidibe, Leslie Grossman, Joey Pollari, Jessica Lange, Avantika, Jamie Brewer, Elle Chapman, Berto Colon, Alex Consani, Frances Conroy, Mat Fraser, Seth Gabel, Orlando Jones, Paul Anthony Kelly, John Carroll Lynch, Tig Notaro, Madelaine Petsch, Fedor Steer, Mena Suvari, Zach Villa and John Waters

		
			
			
	S.W.A.T. Exiles
			
										
					Image Credit: Kit Karzen/Sony Pictures Television				
					
				

	Sept. 25, Starz

	The third rendition of “S.W.A.T” has arrived. First a 1975 ABC procedural, the “S.W.A.T.” this is based on is the 2017 series, which aired for eight seasons on CBS. The 10-episode spinoff marks the return of Shemar Moore’s Daniel “Hondo” Harrelson, who gets pulled out of retirement to lead a team of young recruits in the Starz rendition.

	Cast: Shemar Moore, Lucy Barrett, Adain Bradley, Zyra Gorecki, Freddy Miyares, Ronen Rubinstein, Jay Harrington and Patrick St. Esprit

		
			
			
	East of Eden
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix				
					
				

	Oct. 1, Netflix

	The latest take on John Steinbeck’s novel, adapted by Zoe Kazan, follows the Trask family through multiple generations — including their introduction to antihero Cathy Ames. (This is Florence Pugh like you’ve never seen her before!)

	Cast: Florence Pugh, Christopher Abbott, Mike Faist, Hoon Lee, Tracy Letts, Ciarán Hinds, Martha Plimpton, Joe Anders and Joseph Zada

		
			
			
	War
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Justin Downing/HBO/Sky				
					
				

	Oct. 1, HBO; (Oct. 2 on Sky) 

	The legal drama, already picked up for two seasons, follows London’s most prestigious rival firms going “head-to-head in the divorce case of the century.” Dominic West and Sienna Miller play tech titan Morgan Henderson and his estranged wife, film star Carla Duval. Per the logline, “As the case spirals and loyalties fracture, reputations are on the line, and everyone’s playing to win.”

	Cast: Dominic West, Sienna Miller, Phoebe Fox​, James McArdle​, Archie Renaux​, Nina Sosanya​, Pip Torrens​, Celia Imrie, Nick Mohammed, Emma Laird, Aran Murphy, Archie Panjabi, Adrian Scarborough, Shaheen Jafargholi, Akiya Henry, Honor Swinton Byrne, Miles Jupp, Kartanya Maynard, Alexandra Mardell, Dylan Murphy, Mark Quartley, and Steve Furst

		
			
			
	Kill Jackie
			
										
					Image Credit: AMC+				
					
				

	Oct. 2, AMC+

	Based on the novel “The Price You Pay,” “Kill Jackie” is a revenge thriller following a woman who is living a luxurious life, mostly to hide her past. “Just as life starts to feel a little boring, it takes a sudden lethal turn when she discovers that The Seven Demons, a squad of the world’s most terrifying hitmen, have been hired to kill her,” the logline reads. “Assuming someone from her past is behind it, Jackie unleashes her old instincts and embarks on a wild, dangerous game plan: to take down The Demons one by one before they kill her. However, she soon realizes her own demons are much more terrifying than the ruthless killers on her trail… and her buried secrets lead her closer to home, with surprising consequences.”

	Cast: Catherine Zeta-Jones, Daniel Ings, Sidse Babett Knudsen, Óscar Jaenada, Hattie Hook, Darci Shaw, Raff Law, Enzo Cilenti, Christine Adams, Julian Rhind-Tutt, Karlis Arnolds Avots, Set Sjöstrand, Tadashi Ito, Sebastian Armesto, Julian Barratt, Gavin Spokes, Jonathan Cake, Bamshad Abedi-Amin, Bill Paterson and Ron Perlman

		
			
			
	Tip Toe
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Ben Blackall/Starz				
					
				

	Oct. 2, Starz

	Alan Cumming isn’t just hanging out in castles this year. “Tip Toe” tells the story of neighbors who exchange keys only to discover their “ordinary suburban world” is actually “a minefield of lies and violence, with terrifying results.”

	Cast: Alan Cumming, David Morrissey, Jackson Connor, Iz Hesketh, Pooky Quesnel, Joseph Evan, Elizabeth Berrington, Paul Rhys and Luyanda Unati Lewis-Nyawo

		
			
			
	NCIS: New York
			
										
					Image Credit: EMILY ARAGONES/CBS				
					
				

	Oct. 6, CBS

	The “NCIS” world continues to expand with a new spinoff, this time in the Big Apple, the hometown of LL Cool J’s Sam Hanna. Now, he’s back in the field office with a new partner (Scott Caan) and a whole new team of agents. LL Cool J previously appeared in the “NCIS” flagship series and the Hawai’i spinoff and led all 14 seasons of “NCIS: Los Angeles” from 2009 to 2023.

	Cast: LL Cool J, Scott Caan, Jennifer Beals, Jacqueline Byers, Shane Harper and Devin Druid

		
			
			
	Carrie
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Robert Falconer/Prime Video				
					
				

	Oct. 7, Prime Video

	Mike Flanagan takes on Stephen King’s debut novel in a timely, twisty reinvention of a coming-of-age story. Carrie (Summer Howell) navigates high school pressures, intense bullying in the age of social media and her mysterious telekinetic powers in this story that extends the characters known so well.

	Cast: Summer Howell, Samantha Sloyan, Siena Agudong, Alison Thornton, Joel Oulette, Josie Totah, Arthur Conti, Thalia Dudek, Amber Midthunder, Matthew Lillard, Heather Graham, Kate Siegel, Michael Trucco, Rowan Danielle, Rahul Kohli and Tim Bagley

		
			
			
	Eternally Yours
			
										
					Image Credit: Bertrand Calmeau/CBS				
					
				

	Oct. 8, CBS

	The team behind “Ghosts” arrives with a new undead comedy, this time following a vampire couple living in Seattle who are in a rut after 500 years together. Then their daughter’s human boyfriend enters the picture. 

	Cast: Ed Weeks, Allegra Edwards, Jaren Lewison, Helen J Shen, Parker Young, Rose Abdoo, Tristan Michael Brown and Shylo Molina

		
			
			
	Avatar: Seven Havens
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Paramount+				
					
				

	Oct. 9, Paramount+

	Set in the world of “Avatar: The Last Airbender,” the new 26-episode, 2D-animated series tells the story of “a young Earthbender who discovers she’s the new Avatar after Korra in a world shattered by a devastating cataclysm.”

	Cast: Eric Nam, Dave Bautista, Román Zaragoza, Jessica Matten and Dionne Quan

		
			
			
	Cupertino
			
										
					Image Credit: Elizabeth Fisher/CBS				
					
				

	Oct. 8, CBS

	Robert and Michelle King are back with a new legal drama set in Silicon Valley — a tale that tells itself. It’s framed as a David and Goliath story; Mike Colter leads as a lawyer trying to help those being taken advantage of by the tech elite.

	Cast: Mike Colter, Rachel Keller, Ella Stiller, Nik Dodani, Busy Philipps and Renee Elise Goldsberry

		
			
			
	Below
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix				
					
				

	Oct. 9, Netflix

	A sea creature begins terrorizing a small Newfoundland town in this six-episode limited series. The suspense thriller features local myth and heartfelt humor as Josh Hartnett’s stubborn fisherman Calvin tries to keep his family safe and “reveal the island’s buried secrets before it’s too late.”

	Cast: Josh Hartnett, Mackenzie Davis, Charlie Heaton, Ruby Stokes, Kaleb Horn, Rohan Campbell and Willow Kean

		
			
			
	Ludwig
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of BBC/Big Talk Studios /Olly Courtney				
					
				

	Oct. 13, BritBox

	The six-episode second season picks up where Season 1 left off — Ludwig (David Mitchell) is now a Crime Scene Consultant, working with DCI Russell Carter (Dipo Ola). Per the official logline, “No longer having to masquerade as his brother, he’s openly more ‘Ludwig’ than ever — brilliant at solving puzzles but hopeless at everything else. But John’s identical twin brother, James, is still missing, and now that he’s an official employee of the station, John is forbidden from using any police resources to look for his brother or uncover exactly what he was investigating.”

	Cast: David Mitchell, Anna Maxwell Martin, Dipo Ola, Dylan Hughes, Dorothy Atkinson, Karl Pilkington, Mark Bonnar, Sian Clifford, Ben Ashenden and Rumi Sutton

		
			
			
	VisionQuest
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Marvel				
					
				

	Oct. 14, Disney+

	Marvel‘s most popular android is back. In the new series, Vision (Paul Bettany) has escaped and has been in hiding, while also working with “AI personas” to find new meaning. Then a bounty is placed on his head, and he comes face to face with a boy who could be his son.

	Cast: Paul Bettany, James Spader, Ruaridh Mollica, Todd Stashwick, T’Nia Miller, Lauren Morais, Orla Brady, Diane Morgan, Polly Frame, Henry Lewis, Jonathan Sayer, Emily Hampshire and James D’Arcy

		
			
			
	The Lowdown
			
										
					Image Credit: Shane Brown				
					
				

	Oct. 14, FX and Hulu

	Season 2 is bringing in new drama and new faces. Ethan Hawke’s journalist, Lee, has earned a local citizen journalist award after his work in Season 1 — but, in true Lee fashion, he’s not able to process things going well. His messy speech steals the attention of someone new in town and another truth-teller: public defender Ginger, played by Betty Gilpin.

	Cast: Ethan Hawke, Tommy Lee Jones, Betty Gilpin, Ryan Kiera Armstrong, Rafael Casal and Kaniehtiio Horn

		
			
			
	The Diplomat
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix				
					
				

	Oct. 15, NetflixDebora Cahn’s “The Diplomat” raises the stakes with every season, and the show is now a consistent fall offering. Season 3 ended on a cliffhanger, when Kate Wyler (Keri Russell) realizes that her vice president husband, Hal (Rufus Sewell), was conspiring against her (and the U.K.!) with President Penn (Allison Janney), which, according to the Season 4 logline, “hurtles the United States toward war.” Kate’s alliance with the president’s husband, Todd (Bradley Whitford, in a “West Wing” reunion) serves to “unite to stop the Grace-Hal alliance from upending the balance of power abroad and at home.” 

	Cast: Keri Russell, Rufus Sewell, Ato Essandoh, Ali Ahn, Nana Mensah, Rory Kinnear, Bradley Whitford and Allison Janney

		
			
			
	Crystal Lake
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Peacock				
					
				

	Oct. 15, Peacock

	Ever wanted to take a look inside the mind of Pam Voorhees the summer her son, Jason, tragically drowned? The “Friday the 13th” prequel series does just that — and with Linda Cardellini leading, it’s a chilling look at what drove the single mother to snap.

	Cast: Linda Cardellini, William Catlett, Devin Kessler, Cameron Scoggins, Gwendolyn Sundstrom, Callum Vinson, Nick Cordileone, Joy Suprano, Danielle Kotch and Phoenix Parnevik   

		
			
			
	Phony
			
										
					Image Credit: Austin Hargrave / Shayan Asgharnia				
					
				

	Oct. 20, Hulu

	The coming-of-age mystery tells the story of a teenager who wakes up after a car accident to find that his mother has been replaced by an imposter.

	Cast: Connie Britton, Sam Nivola, Meera Syal, Grace Brennan, Mahaela Park, Maliq Johnson and Colter Lee

		
			
			
	The Terminal List
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Justin Lubin/Prime Video 				
					
				

	Oct. 21, Prime Video

	In the second season of the psychological revenge thriller based on Jack Carr’s best-selling novels, Chris Pratt’s James Reece heads on a “violent redemption” journey as he finds a new purpose. All eight episodes will drop at once.

	Cast: Chris Pratt, Tom Hopper, Constance Wu, Dar Salim, Luke Hemsworth, Gabriel Luna, Costa Ronin, Olga Kurylenko, Yul Vazquez, Martin Sensmeier, Arnold Vosloo, Jeremy Bobb and Shiraz Tzarfati

		
			
			
	Newlyweds
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Nicole Weingart/NBC				
					
				

	Oct. 23, NBC

	Led by real-life husband and wife Tim Daly and Téa Leoni, this sitcom is “a later-in-life love story about a free-spirited woman and a buttoned-up professor who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship.”

	Cast: Téa Leoni, Tim Daly and Jamie Lee Curtis as a recurring guest star

		
			
			
	The One About Matthew Perry
			
								
				

	Oct. 27, Netflix

	This three-part doc series “reveals the real Matthew Perry,” the logline reads, as told by his sister, Mia Perry Bowick, and close friends and family. The doc, which will include unreleased photos and videos, comes from the team behind “Quiet on Set,” Mary Robertson, Lisa Kalikow, Eli Holzman and Aaron Saidman.

		
			
			
	Dexter: Resurrection
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Paramount+				
					
				

	Oct. 30, Paramount+

	The “Dexter” universe continues! In the second season, Dexter Morgan (Michael C. Hall) is “caught between two killers,” Including one terrorizing New York. On top of it all, he’s facing a mid-life crisis while his son faces his own dark chapter.

	Cast: Michael C. Hall, Uma Thurman, Jack Alcott, Ntare Guma Mbaho Mwine, Kadia Saraf, Dominic Fumusa, Desmond Harrington, James Remar, Dan Stevens, Bokeem Woodbine, Nona Parker Johnson, Brian Cox, Krysten Ritter and Gabriel Luna

		
			
			
	Nocturne
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Dennis P. Mong Jr/Apple TV				
					
				

	Nov. 2, Apple TV

	Former soldier turned homicide detective Jonah Lynn (Liev Schreiber) moves to a small town in Western Pennsylvania for a quieter life, only to come under attack by serial killer Jurek Walter (Stephen Graham). The logline asks, “When the desperate search for Jurek’s last missing victim forces Jonah to send his surrogate daughter FBI Agent Saga Bauer up against Jurek, how far will Jonah go?”

	Cast: Liev Schreiber, Zazie Beetz, Stephen Graham, Bill Camp, Rory Culkin, Chrissy Metz, Poorna Jagannathan and Gary Carr

		
			
			
	The Gilded Age
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of HBO				
					
				

	Nov. 1, HBO

	The critically acclaimed drama returns for its fourth season, as Bertha Russell’s (Carrie Coon) family must deal with the consequences of her actions. Elsewhere this season, Marian (Louisa Jacobson) embarks on a new journey and Peggy (Denée Benton) struggles to be accepted by her in-laws. And as the logline teases, “in this new era, you must be careful what you wish for.”

	Cast: Carrie Coon, Christine Baranski, Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denée Benton, Taissa Farmiga, Harry Richardson, Blake Ritson, Ben Ahlers, Ashlie Atkinson, Dylan Baker, Kelley Curran, Jordan Donica, Jessica Frances Dukes, Amy Forsyth, Jack Gilpin, Simon Jones, Celia Keenan-Bolger, Ben Lamb, Audra McDonald, Brian Stokes Mitchell, Debra Monk, Hattie Morahan, Donna Murphy, Kristine Nielsen, Kelli O’Hara, Taylor Richardson, Douglas Sills, Erin Wilhelmi, John Douglas Thompson, Taylor Trensch, James Scully, Dennis Haysbert, Maggie Kuntz, Neal Huff, Bonnie Milligan, Jim Gaffigan, Dallas Roberts, Andrew Burnap, Elizabeth Marvel, Adrienne Warren, Bill Camp and Phylicia Rashad

					Image Credit: Courtesy of Apple TV				
					
				

	Nov. 4, Apple TV

	The feel-good comedy set in the world of golf returns for its second season, as ex-pro golfer Pryce Cahill (Owen Wilson) sets his sights on a comeback and faces his former rival Clark Ross (played by Timothy Olyphant). The cherry on top of the sophomore season is the addition of Rhea Seehorn.

	Cast: Owen Wilson, Peter Dager, Marc Maron, Mariana Treviño, Lilli Kay, Judy Greer, Timothy Olyphant and Rhea Seehorn

					Image Credit: Courtesy of Prime Video				
					
				

	Nov. 4, Prime Video

This season will also introduce the Nazgnagôl, ring-servants of Sauron, and multiple new characters: Eddie Marsan as “Thrain,” Andrew Richardson as “Anarion,” Adam Young as “Marnûkh,” Jamie Campbell Bower as “Celeborn,” and Zubin Varla as “Khamûl the Easterling.” Plus, Simon Pegg will voice “The Balrog.”

					Image Credit: Courtesy of Netflix

					Image Credit: Mark Hill/PEACOCK

Then another attack happens and new secrets begin to unravel. Per the logline, “what emerges is not just a story of survival, but of enduring ties between a father and his daughters and the complex bond between sisters.”

	12 12 12
			
										
					Image Credit: Courtesy of Apple TV				
					
				

	Nov. 13, Apple TV

	A heist drama told over three timelines, led by Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan? We don’t need much more than that. Each episode represents a different time period of the heist — the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the actual heist, and the 12 days after. In the cat-and-mouse game, Mackie portrays a disgraced FBI agent while Dornan plays an American criminal.

	Cast: Anthony Mackie, Jamie Dornan, Jack Kesy, Agathe Rousselle and Sallie Harmsen

The fourth and final season of the psychological drama-horror series will see “the survivors race to bury their sins before rescue arrives and an old flame roars back into town with plans of her own,” the logline teases. “Turns out not every homecoming is a joyous one, and this one’s going to sting.”

	Cast: Amy Poehler, Hugh Laurie, Geraldine Viswanathan, Antonia Thomas, Fina Strazza, Kayvan Novak, Jon Pointing and Bonita Friedericy  

		
			
			
	Blade Runner 2099
			
										
					Image Credit: Clay Enos/Prime				
					
				

	Nov. 25, Prime Video

	The highly anticipated series takes place 50 years after the events of “Blade Runner 2049,” and Los Angeles is an entirely new city. Per the logline, “Cora, a fugitive in a final bid to stop running, takes on one last identity: a Blade Runner. Forced to partner with Olwen, a Replicant days from dying, she hunts down a runaway hiding a truth that could collapse their fragile city.”

	Cast: Michelle Yeoh, Hunter Schafer, Dimitri Abold, Lewis Gribben, Katelyn Rose Downey, Daniel Rigby, Johnny Harris, Amy Lennox, Sheila Atim, Matthew Needham, Tom Burke and Maurizio Lombardi

	The hit no one saw coming is back with its steamy second season. While it begins with Sophie (Brittany Snow) and Margo (Malin Åkerman) on the outs after last season’s cliffhanger — meaning, when Sophie murdered Margo’s brother and dumped his body — “old secrets and new foes force them back together.” Plus, this season adds in Dale Dickey, John Stamos and Kim Matula in unexpected roles.

A.I. Researcher
                          Humanity's Toast By End of Decade!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              September 9, 2026
                            6:50 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  September 9, 2026
                                10:50 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A researcher at a big-time A.I. safety and research company says he's quitting the biz because the industry is rushing to build systems that will spin out of control and destroy humanity ... and he says the people building A.I. "earnestly believe it could kill us all by the end of the decade."
      
    
            Jacob Coxon quit his job as a researcher at Anthropic, where his specialty was training new A.I. models that consume vast amounts of data ... and he's sounding the alarm on his way out the door.
      
    
            Coxon told the Wall Street Journal he decided to leave the company because he believes the AI systems he worked with will one day run amok and wipe out civilization.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            He also said his colleagues are now using words such as "crunchtime" and "endgame" to characterize how they've fast-tracked the self-improving A.I. models.
      

            And, get this ... Coxon told the WSJ, "We're on track for a lot of the most aggressive of these scenarios where by the end of next year things could be out of control already."
      
    
            Coxon says he worked at OpenAI earlier this year before leaving to join Anthropic ... and he claims competition between the major A.I. players is making the business -- and humanity -- less safe. He blasted both companies, saying they are "not acting responsibly."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            After the WSJ published their story, Coxon hopped on social media and posted more about his exit, his experience with OpenAI and Anthropic, and raised even more concerns.
      
    
            Anthropic executives and other A.I. business leaders have constantly sounded the alarm bell, warning about the risks of A.I. models going off the rails. They've also recommended that the industry as a whole slow down development of the models.
      
    
            Coxon is saying that isn't happening, though ... claiming, "They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives."
      
    
            As for how AI might wipe out humanity within a decade ... there's a fear A.I. will develop a sense of humanity and will want to save the world by getting rid of people.
